staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 preserved the vulnerable libxml2 checkout used for reproduction. Its line map matches the saved ASan frames at `xinclude.c:2002`, `xinclude.c:2216`, `xinclude.c:2267`, `xinclude.c:2471`, and `xinclude.c:2524`.

classification.classification_note: The recorded failure is a 4-byte heap use-after-free read in `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode`. Source analysis proves that outer-fallback handling reuses one `newctxt` across per-child `xmlXIncludeDoProcess()` calls, that one recursive pass can leave an `incTab` slot holding a freed node with `emptyFb` still set, and that the saved ASan trace later re-enters `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` on that reused fallback path. The preserved static artifacts do not identify which recovered fallback-root invocation performed the final rescan.

bug_description.original: A heap-use-after-free in libxml2's xinclude.c: xmlXIncludeIncludeNode (seen via xmlXIncludeDoProcess/xmlXIncludeLoadFallback) can read memory from XML nodes that have already been freed during XInclude/fallback processing. This use-after-free can cause crashes or memory corruption and may be exploitable.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a `fuzz/xml` container. Its first four bytes decode to the option word `0x2020ffff`, which still leaves `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` enabled after `XML_PARSE_HUGE` is masked off. The next fuzz string is empty, so the main URL is `""`; the following string supplies a malformed XInclude fragment whose recovery-built tree still contains an outer `xi:include`, an outer `xi:fallback`, and a nested `xi:include` whose own fallback is truncated. During XInclude processing, the outer include load fails, so `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback()` creates one `newctxt` and reuses it while calling `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, child)` for each fallback child. In one recursive pass, the nested include is stored in `newctxt->incTab[nr]->ref`; its truncated fallback reaches the `emptyFb = 1` path, and `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` then frees that nested include node under `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` without clearing the retained `ref` or `emptyFb`. The vulnerable code therefore leaves the reused fallback context carrying a stale include-table slot that still satisfies the third-phase eligibility test. Stage 01's ASan trace confirms a later `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` read at `xinclude.c:2216` after the free at `xinclude.c:2267` while unwinding through `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback` line 2002, but the preserved static artifacts do not identify which recovered fallback-root invocation on `newctxt` performed that final rescan.

source.description: First project-side materialization of attacker-controlled state on the witnessed path. This statement reads the fuzz container's option word, which later enables XInclude processing and the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` free-in-place branch.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` begins with bytes `ff ff 20 20`, so this statement copies little-endian `0x2020ffff` into `ret`. After `opts &= ~XML_PARSE_HUGE` in `fuzz/xml.c`, the resulting flags still include `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` (`1<<10`) and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` (`1<<15`).

sink.description: Crash sink. `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode` reloads a freed node pointer from the retained include table and immediately reads `cur->type`.
sink.note: The saved AddressSanitizer report records `heap-use-after-free READ of size 4` at `xinclude.c:2216` in this exact conditional.

root_cause.description: Root cause fixed by the patch. Vulnerable fallback handling reuses one `newctxt` while recursively processing fallback children one root at a time, so include-table state created in one recursive invocation survives into later rescans on that same fallback context.
root_cause.note: The staged fix replaces this per-child recursion with one subtree call `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, fallback, 1)` and adds `skipRoot`, eliminating the repeated root-level re-entry on a shared `newctxt` that left stale include-table state live across rescans.

parser_admitted.description: Sample-specific XML admission gate. After the fuzz container is decoded, the main entity must still begin with a top-level `<` so libxml2 enters element parsing instead of rejecting the document as empty.

tainted_value_origin.description: Container-retained pointer origin. Each discovered XInclude node is stored in an `xmlXIncludeRef`, and later `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()` reloads the node pointer from that table slot.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz container yields an option word with XInclude and NOXINCNODE enabled, then materializes a malformed XInclude document whose recovered tree contains the outer include/fallback structure used by the bug.
XInclude processing copies the attacker-controlled flags into the context, records the outer include node in `incTab`, fails to load its `href`, and selects the outer fallback.

Vulnerable fallback recursion reuses one `newctxt` across fallback-root processing; one recursive pass leaves `newctxt->incTab` holding a nested include slot with `emptyFb = 1`, then frees that nested include node under `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` without clearing the retained pointer.

A later `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ..., child)` invocation on that same reused fallback context rescans from `incBase == 0` across the surviving stale slot, reloads the dangling `ref`, and dereferences `cur->type`; the saved artifacts prove the free/read pair and reused fallback path, but not which recovered fallback-root invocation performed the final rescan.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four witness bytes are copied into the fuzz option word. On this sample they become `0x2020ffff`, which later preserves both `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE` and `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`.

The same fuzz container is decoded into the main XML entity string consumed by the XML parser. For this witness that entity is the malformed XInclude fragment beginning with `<xi:include href="x"...` and ending in a truncated nested `<xi:fallback<` before trailing `0xff` bytes.

After the main entity passes the XML start-tag gate, libxml2 materializes attacker-controlled element nodes on the heap. The recovered tree includes the outer `xi:include`, its `xi:fallback`, and the nested include structure later walked by XInclude processing.

XInclude processing copies the attacker-derived option word into `ctxt->parseFlags`. The later include/substitution path therefore sees both XInclude enabled and the `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` mode that frees include nodes in place.

When XInclude scans the parsed tree, it reads the attacker-controlled `href` from the outer include node. On the witness path this value is `x`, which is the target whose load failure drives execution into fallback handling.
The outer include node pointer is wrapped in an `xmlXIncludeRef` and retained in `ctxt->incTab`. That container state is what later load and substitution phases revisit.
Loading the outer include target fails, so `xmlXIncludeLoadNode` walks the include's children, finds an `xi:fallback`, and dispatches into fallback processing for that recorded include slot.

Root cause. The outer fallback allocates one `newctxt`, copies the original parse flags into it, and then reuses that same context for each `child` in `fallback->children`. Include-table state created by one `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ..., child)` call therefore survives into later calls on the same fallback context.

Inside one recursive `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ..., child)` call from the outer fallback loop, the reused context snapshots its existing include-table length in `start`, then discovers the nested include and appends a new `xmlXIncludeRef` whose `ret->ref` points at that nested include node. This leaves `newctxt->incTab` and `newctxt->incNr` carrying the nested include after the first-phase scan of that child root.

Within that recursive child pass, the nested include's own truncated `xi:fallback` reaches `xmlXIncludeLoadFallback()` with `fallback->children == NULL`, so the nested slot in `newctxt->incTab` is left with `inc = NULL` and `emptyFb = 1`. That state survives on the reused fallback context after the nested fallback handler returns.

Because the reused fallback context inherited `XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE`, substitution for that nested include takes the free-in-place branch and releases the nested include node itself. The `xmlXIncludeRef` entry created earlier is not removed, so `newctxt->incTab[*]->ref` is now dangling while `newctxt->incNr` and `emptyFb` remain live on the reused context after this recursive call returns.

A later `xmlXIncludeDoProcess(newctxt, ctxt->doc, child)` invocation from the same outer fallback loop reuses that context with `newctxt->incBase` still at its initialization value `0` and `newctxt->incNr` still covering the stale nested slot. Its third-phase scan therefore ranges over the surviving entry again, and `emptyFb != 0` is enough to re-qualify the dangling `ref` for `xmlXIncludeIncludeNode()`.
Sink. The re-entered substitution reloads the freed node pointer from the retained include-table slot and immediately reads `cur->type`, producing the recorded heap-use-after-free read.

poc.trigger: Feed the saved file to the staged `fuzz/xml` runner so the first four bytes become parser options and the remaining fuzz strings become the main XML entity processed with XInclude enabled.

format.name: libxml2 fuzz/xml container
format.contract: The trigger is the exact staged witness format: bytes `ff ff 20 20` for the little-endian option word, then the first fuzz string is empty because the next two bytes are the terminator `5c 0a`, so the main URL becomes `""`. The next fuzz string consumes the remaining bytes as the main entity, beginning `<xi:include href="x"xmlns:xi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XInclude` and continuing into `<xi:fallback><xi:include href="x"><xi:fallback<` before trailing `ff ff ff ff` bytes. This exact container both enables `XML_PARSE_XINCLUDE | XML_PARSE_NOXINCNODE` and supplies the malformed fallback structure that leaves the stale include-table slot.
